title: Fern Hollow bridge: corrosion, missed maintenance action, fracture-critical identification, and oversight failure
summary: Fern Hollow is encoded as inspection/maintenance action-lag and fracture-critical visibility: corrosion and section loss, clogged drains, repeated maintenance recommendations, incorrect inspection/load-rating surfaces, and oversight gaps combined before collapse.

status_history.note: Added as civil/structural failure lane record.

claims.claim: The NTSB page records that the Fern Hollow bridge collapsed on January 28, 2022, after a transverse tie plate failed because of corrosion and section loss; the bridge fell about 100 feet.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB page records clogged drains and repeated maintenance recommendations, making the case an action-lag record rather than an invisible-hazard-only record.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB probable-cause/contributing-factor statement includes failure to act on maintenance recommendations, poor inspections, incomplete fracture-critical member identification, incorrect load ratings, and insufficient PennDOT oversight.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The record is encoded as an inspection/maintenance-governance failure because corrosion evidence, drainage defects, fracture-critical status, and load-rating/oversight surfaces did not produce adequate correction before collapse.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.incident_class: highway bridge collapse from corrosion-related member failure
type_payload.system: steel bridge, transverse tie plates, drainage, inspection, maintenance, load-rating and oversight program

sequence_of_events.event: Corrosion and section loss degraded a transverse tie plate.
Drainage and maintenance recommendations were present but not effectively corrected.
Structural member failed and bridge collapsed.
NTSB traced inspection, fracture-critical identification, load rating, maintenance, and oversight failures.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Transverse tie-plate failure due to corrosion and section loss.
latent_conditions: maintenance backlog/action-lag allowed known degradation to persist
inspection classification did not make critical member vulnerability visible enough
oversight did not convert repeated signals into correction
